paper_metadata.title: Implementing Credit Risk Analysis with Quantum Singular Value Transformation

experiments.description: End-to-end simulation of VaR estimation using a QSVT-based state preparation operator combined with iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) on a 4-counterparty credit risk instance.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with QSVT-based state preparation for VaR
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative bisection search until the estimated VaR converges to the target confidence level; IQAE run with specified precision and confidence parameters

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Counterparty default scenarios are encoded in an n-qubit counterparties register C; the total loss is loaded into the amplitude of a target qubit T via controlled Ry rotations; QSVT is then applied to filter scenarios below a loss threshold.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the cumulative distribution function F(L_T) = Pr(L <= L_T) and use bisection search to infer VaR_{alpha_var}(L) = inf{x in R | F_x(L) >= 1 - alpha_var}.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold filtering via polynomial approximation of an even threshold function T_mu and post-selection on registers T and B being |0⟩.

problem_instance.description: Multivariate Gaussian conditional independence credit risk instance with 4 counterparties and correlated risk factors; VaR estimated from aggregated losses.

dataset_specification.description: Input values are described as originating from a suitably anonymized and perturbed database containing real, not synthetic, data; no public dataset name or date range reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Gaussian risk factors truncated at ±2; 2 qubits per Gaussian variable; scenario probabilities reconstructed from the uncertainty operator U; classical benchmark CDF computed from simulated scenario probabilities.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation campaign over multiple target loss values; CDF values compared against a classical benchmark; VaR obtained via iterative bisection search; number of shots reported as 2048.

implementation_details.framework_version: QSPPACK library (MATLAB-based) for polynomial coefficients and phase estimation; Python implementation for end-to-end algorithm
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute polynomial approximation of the threshold function using QSPPACK; estimate QSVT phases; reconstruct scenario probabilities from the uncertainty operator U; classically compute benchmark CDF values; set bisection-search thresholds.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale measured probabilities by k^2; compare QSVT CDF estimates to classical benchmark; use bisection search to convert CDF estimates into VaR.

speedup_claims.conditions: for amplitude estimation / QAE-based risk analysis in the asymptotic regime
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speed-up is theoretical; practical implementation is limited by circuit cost, polynomial approximation degree, and rescaling factor k^2.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: previous multi-risk-factor quantum credit-risk circuits with exponential gate growth
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims linear scaling in the number of counterparties n, but notes that the dependence of d on precision and n remains to be proved.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(d n) for the QSVT-based state preparation circuit depth; IQAE complexity O(epsilon_IQAE^-1 log(alpha_IQAE^-1 log2(epsilon_IQAE^-1)))
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Constant-factor overhead from k^2 rescaling and polynomial approximation degree d

experiments.description: Simulation of the CDF estimation subroutine alone, benchmarking QSVT-based estimates against classically reconstructed benchmark CDF values for multiple target losses.

algorithm.variant: QSVT-based CDF estimation circuit used as state preparation for IQAE

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The probability of each default scenario is encoded in the amplitudes of register C; the threshold condition is implemented by QSVT acting on the amplitude-loaded target qubit T.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Pr(L <= L_T) for a range of target losses L_T.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Polynomial approximation of an even threshold function T_mu; post-selection on registers T and B being |0⟩.

problem_instance.description: Same 4-counterparty credit risk instance as the main VaR experiment, evaluated at multiple target loss thresholds.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Benchmark CDF values obtained by simulating the original uncertainty operator U and reconstructing scenario probabilities classically.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Benchmarking table comparing QSVT CDF estimates to classical benchmark CDF values across multiple target losses.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute the benchmark CDF by simulating the uncertainty operator U and classically aggregating scenario probabilities.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare QSVT CDF outputs to benchmark values; note that values above 1 arise from k^2 rescaling.

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment is a benchmarking study of CDF estimates; no runtime or asymptotic speedup is reported.

experiments.description: Iterative bisection-search experiment for VaR estimation using the QSVT-based CDF oracle on the same 4-counterparty instance.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid quantum-classical VaR estimation via bisection search with IQAE/QSVT CDF oracle
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Bisection search converges toward the expected VaR value; stopping rule not explicitly quantified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The quantum circuit provides CDF estimates for candidate loss thresholds; the classical outer loop updates low/current/high levels in a bisection search.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the loss threshold corresponding to the desired VaR confidence level alpha_var.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Classical bisection search over target loss values using quantum-estimated CDF as the feasibility test.

problem_instance.description: VaR search on the same 4-asset credit risk instance, with target value shown in Figure 5 at 54,807 dollars.

dataset_specification.description: Same anonymized and perturbed real-data-derived instance as the main experiment.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same as the main VaR experiment; bisection search uses the quantum CDF oracle repeatedly.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Iterative bisection search visualized over iterations; convergence compared against classically estimated target VaR.

implementation_details.framework_version: Python implementation; QSPPACK used for QSVT polynomial/phase synthesis
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Initialize low/current/high bisection bounds and target loss.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Update bisection bounds based on measured CDF estimates until convergence.

speedup_claims.conditions: when using IQAE as the amplitude-estimation subroutine inside the hybrid bisection-search VaR workflow
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper demonstrates convergence in simulation, but does not report wall-clock runtime or an empirical speedup factor.
